items.title: Al Vollmer interviewed by Monk Rowe, New Hartford, New York, June 8, 2017
items.q: So I remember Albert Burbank and he said, “What is your name?” And I said, “My name is Al for Albert.”

ctx.x: But I mean also because of the dentistry I was able to help many of the musicians. I’ve had incredible patients. I mean I’ll just give one little story. How I started, before I got involved and had the big house, I belonged to the Connecticut Traditional Jazz Club, which was formed by Bill Bissonnette, who was a trombonist and a absolute rabid New Orleans — nothing is any good if it’s not from New Orleans. Anyway, he had his own band and he couldn’t run a club and put on the concerts and all that, so he put out a…

upper denture drops down and it’s very embarrassing.” And I said, “I can take care of that. We’ll reline your denture.” So I did. I relined his denture and they were happy. I helped Louie Nelson, I helped Andrew Morgan. Those were the New Orleans guys. And once Punch Miller was staying at Bill Bissonnette’s house in Bridgeport, Connecticut, which is about an hour, little more than an hour away from me.
